Project configuration reference

Source: vignettes/configuration.Rmd
configuration.Rmd

Use this reference to look up a YAML setting, understand which files a build will touch, or restore a saved result. For a first build, follow the getting started guide.

The project root and profiles

Run the first build from the analysis project. If it has no base configuration, projr creates _projr.yml with explicit paths for raw-data (_raw_data), output (_output), cache (_tmp), and docs (docs). Existing scripts using those folders can keep their paths. If your files are already elsewhere, point the corresponding label at the existing folder. Once a base file exists, its directory declarations determine which labels are available.

File When it applies
_projr.yml Base configuration shared by the project.
_projr-<profile>.yml Overrides for a named analysis or machine.
_projr-local.yml Local overrides with highest precedence.

Each file can live at the project root or in .projr/config/. When both locations contain the same filename, the root copy wins. All relative paths in either location start at the project root. A nested script can therefore use the same directory labels when run in RStudio or during a build.

Select profiles with a build’s profile argument or PROJR_PROFILE. For example, Sys.setenv(PROJR_PROFILE = "site-a,cluster") applies both named profiles, with the earlier name taking precedence when both specify a value. Local overrides still win. Use projr_yml_get() to inspect the merged settings, projr_yml_get("default") to inspect the base file, and projr_yml_check() to validate the active configuration.

Choosing the checkout for a build

The first interactive build names the full project root and asks once for permission to run its scripts and hooks, write its configured files, and perform the requested Git and archive operations. Configured directories can be outside the checkout. Approval is remembered for that checkout’s path in the user’s projr configuration directory. A fresh clone at another path prompts again, even if it contains the same _projr.yml.

For unattended builds, pass the root of the checkout as project. Use projr_build(project = ".", archive_github = TRUE) when the job starts at that root, or pass the path to the root from another working directory. The explicit path authorizes this invocation. Git and remote destinations still use their own credentials.

Files projr keeps

The .projr/ folder belongs to the project. Git can track its configuration and manifests so a fresh checkout knows which files belonged to a build. The production build history goes in .projr/BUILDLOG.md and can be committed with the analysis. Detailed logs for individual runs stay local in .projr/logs/.

A build or restore moves recognized configuration files and manifests from the earlier _projr/ layout. Read-only queries still work on older checkouts. If both locations contain the same configuration filename or a manifest store, projr stops before moving anything so you can choose which history to keep. Existing logs in a former cache directory remain readable with projr_log_view(log_file = "...").

Directory declarations

This example keeps incoming data and generated figures where they already live. It also creates a deliverable containing the figures and the rendered documents.

directories:
  raw-data:
    path: incoming/site-a
  cache:
    path: scratch
  docs:
    path: reports/rendered
  output-figures:
    path: results/figures
  output-delivery:
    path: deliverables
    include: [output-figures, docs]

After a production build, the included copies are under deliverables/output-figures/ and deliverables/docs/. Each copy reflects the current source, including file removals. Other files in the receiving directory are separate from these copies. An output can include another assembled output. Cycles, paths that would copy a directory inside itself, and overlapping paths that could erase an input are rejected.

For R package datasets, projr_path_get("data", "sample.rda", safe = FALSE) resolves to data/sample.rda in the project root. The data label is built in and its location is fixed. A production build copies datasets staged by projr_use_data(sample) into data/ and internal datasets into R/sysdata.rda. Development builds keep staged datasets under the configured cache. If an active directory label already uses data/ or a subdirectory such as data/site-a/, the helper reports that label before saving. Projects that store their own files there can still build and look up those paths.

directories.<label> field Meaning
path Required for configurable labels. An absolute path can point outside the checkout.
hash Include the directory in the version history. Defaults to true for raw data, outputs and docs, and false for cache.
include On an output label, list declared raw, docs or output labels to copy under their label names. An empty list requests no includes.
output Older source-side form. Use an output label or list to copy into those outputs, true for all other outputs, or false to skip.
package On an output label, true also builds the R source package and copies it under pkg/.
license A license identifier such as CC-BY, or a mapping containing type, authors and year. See vignette("directory-licenses").
ignore Controls both Git and R build rules. Defaults to false for package datasets (data) and true for other declared directories, including raw-data. Accepts YAML booleans, ignore, no-ignore, or manual.
ignore-git, ignore-rbuild Set either type separately. When ignore is also supplied, the choices must agree.
ignore-even-if-inactive Defaults to true. Applies that profile’s enabled ignore types while a different profile is active.

Use a raw, cache or output prefix when a label should participate in the corresponding build stage, for example raw-site-a and output-tables. Declare a cache for builds that need staging, and docs for collected documents. If several cache labels are configured, the first supplies the build cache. Labels used as directory lookups need a declared path, including code and data if your scripts use those names. The suffix -empty is reserved for archive metadata.

projr_path_get("output-figures", "plot.png") returns a filename and creates its parent if needed. projr_path_get_dir("output-figures") returns a directory. Use create = FALSE for lookup only. Both accept format = "absolute", "relative", or "auto" (the default follows the YAML path’s format). Relative results are usable from the caller’s working directory. The default safe = TRUE allows projr to route output and document writes to the build’s working area. Use safe = FALSE to address the configured final location directly. Literal paths in your own code use R’s working directory.

When refreshing ignores, projr considers each profile’s configured paths. If any eligible profile requests a Git ignore, the project keeps that rule. R package build ignores follow the same rule when the root has a DESCRIPTION. Changing a path removes the old generated rule once its last qualifying reference disappears. User-written rules outside the managed section stay in place. Only paths inside the checkout generate rules, so a Windows path in an inactive profile can coexist with a Linux checkout.

Initialization keeps the contents of an existing .gitignore outside the projr-managed section, including comments, duplicate rules and exceptions. It also adds editable defaults for R session files, .vdoc.*, .DS_Store and Thumbs.db. You can delete those defaults after initialization.

Documents, R scripts and hooks

Setting Selection
build.scripts Ordered inputs for a production build. Also used by dev builds when dev.scripts is absent.
dev.scripts Ordered inputs for a development build. The scripts argument to projr_build_dev() takes precedence.
build.hooks, dev.hooks Each accepts pre, post, and both. Supply R script paths under the stage. Dev and production hooks are configured independently.

A script selection accepts .R, .Rmd and .qmd paths or glob patterns. To skip files, add an item such as - exclude: reports/draft.Rmd to either scripts list. Each exclude takes one path or glob pattern. Quoted strings such as "!reports/draft.Rmd" also work. Matches within a glob are alphabetical. Exclusions apply to the selection as a whole. If every entry is an exclusion, projr uses automatic discovery and skips the matching files. For example, scripts: [{exclude: scratch.R}] builds the project first and then runs the other top-level R scripts. In a directory without a rendering project, the remaining documents and scripts run together alphabetically. Overlapping globs select each file once. Repeating a literal R script or standalone document runs it again. An explicit scripts: [], or scripts = character() in R, skips document rendering and script execution.

For example, suppose a Quarto project has the following selection.

build:
  scripts: [prepare.R, intro.qmd, check-data.R, results.qmd, summarise.R]
  hooks:
    post: hooks/record-build.R

Here prepare.R and check-data.R run first. Quarto builds intro.qmd and results.qmd together when the selection reaches results.qmd. Then summarise.R runs. Projr temporarily sets Quarto’s project.render (and book.chapters for a book), or Bookdown’s rmd_files. It keeps the selected configuration through post-build hooks, then restores the original YAML, including on failure. For Quarto document exclusions this also covers active profile and included configuration files inside the checkout. A Quarto book needs its index page whenever it renders any remaining chapters. An R-only selection runs just those scripts. Documents for a different engine render individually in their listed positions. Choose one project configuration when both _quarto.yml and _bookdown.yml are present.

When script selection is omitted, projr builds the Quarto or Bookdown project using its own settings and then runs top-level R scripts alphabetically. In a directory without a rendering project it runs top-level documents and scripts together in alphabetical order. Automatic R discovery skips configured hooks, underscore-prefixed scripts and renv_repos.R.

Renderers retain their own working-directory conventions, including Quarto’s execute-dir and R Markdown’s knit_root_dir. To pass options from R, use args_engine in the build call. Group options by engine when the selection mixes engines. See options for a build engine.

The collected document and its companion assets stay together. Where basenames collide, projr preserves the affected documents’ project-relative subdirectories. Renderer intermediates such as generated TeX files receive project-relative ignore rules, including for nested source documents.

Builds, dependencies and versions

Setting Values and effect
build.renv auto (default) snapshots when the project has renv.lock or renv/activate.R. true requests snapshots even for a first lockfile. false disables build snapshots. A production build checks dependencies before rendering and snapshots again without prompting afterward.
build.git A boolean, or a mapping with booleans commit, add-untracked, and push. The first build writes false when there is no Git checkout, or disables push when the branch has no upstream. For an existing configuration with these settings omitted the normal production defaults enable all three.
build.restrictions.branch true allows any branch (default), a name or list allows those branches, and false or [] allows none.
build.restrictions.not_behind_git Defaults to true. Checks whether the local Git branch is behind its upstream. Existing configurations can use not_behind.
build.restrictions.not_behind_remote Defaults to true. Checks the archives selected for publication, including one-off archives. Set false to skip archive version checks or supply the titles of the archives to check.
build.restrictions.rule base_version_not_behind (or base, the default) checks the last completed local version and the proposed version. target_version_not_behind (or target) checks just the proposed version.
build.cite A boolean or a mapping of booleans cff, inst-citation, and codemeta. Selects citation files for production build updates.
metadata.version-format Defaults to major.minor.patch-dev. Supported formats also allow major.minor or major before the development component, a dot separator before it, and a final 1 or 9000 in place of dev.
parameters Project-specific values available inside scripts, for example parameters: {seed: 42} and projr_par_get("seed").

Use projr_build_dev() to iterate. It preserves the current project version and can run before the project has one. An unversioned project stages its working files in <cache>/projr/dev/. The @version placeholder requires a version set by a production build or by projr_version_set(). Use old_dev_remove = FALSE to keep older working directories. Use projr_build_patch(), projr_build_minor() or projr_build_major() to choose the component for a versioned build. msg records a build description. clear_output accepts "pre", "post" or "never". Production builds default to "pre" and development builds to "never". Pass clear_output = NULL to read PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT. For console and file logging, profile environment files, and authentication, see vignette("environment").

If you add a package DESCRIPTION to an existing renv analysis, renv can choose a new library when the next R session starts. When that library is empty apart from renv, builds reuse the populated analysis library for this checkout. The build and its renderers use the same packages. A populated new library takes precedence, and explicit renv library settings are respected. A missing renderer dependency stops the build with the package names and the installation command for the project library.

Archive version checks

Before a production build publishes, projr shows the last completed version in the checkout, the proposed build version, and the version recorded by each selected archive. A new or empty archive passes. For an existing archive the proposed version must be newer than its last successful upload. By default the checkout must also be at least as recent as that upload.

The local base comes from the latest build recorded in .projr/BUILDLOG.md. For an older checkout without a recorded build, projr can use its stable project version. A development version alone does not establish a completed build.

The archive records its completed project version after all selected directories have uploaded. If a populated archive has missing or unreadable version information, the build stops so you can inspect it before publishing.

For example, suppose your checkout last built 0.1.0 and the archive already contains 0.2.0. The default rule stops even if you request a major build to 1.0.0. Choose rule: target when you intend to publish that version from the older checkout. Both rules stop a proposed build of 0.2.0, since the archive already has that version.

By default projr checks the destinations this build is scheduled to publish to, including those requested with archive_github or archive_local. To check specific archives on every production build, list their configured titles. This also checks registered archives that the build only reads.

build:
  restrictions:
    not_behind_remote: [reports, backup]
    rule: target

If the same title appears under both remotes.github and remotes.local, write it as <type>:<title>, for example not_behind_remote: [github:reports]. Set not_behind_remote: false to skip archive checks. Git upstream checks have their own not_behind_git setting. Development builds skip both checks.

Hashing and history 

settings:
  hashing:
    approach: cpp
    cores: 1

cpp streams files through the native implementation. legacy uses the historical R hashing method. Both produce the same file MD5s and use the same directory histories. cores is a positive integer. Increase it to distribute files across workers during a hashing phase. The default uses a single worker. The earlier settings.hash-engine spelling is accepted for compatibility.

Each production build records its selected inputs before rendering and its outputs afterward. Each directory has its own history. For example, a change in output adds a new file list for that directory while raw-data can keep using its existing list. Development builds leave these histories alone.

Where to look Where the history for raw-data lives
Project checkout .projr/manifests/raw-data/
Local archive manifests/raw-data/ inside the archive folder
GitHub Release The raw-data/ directory inside the manifest.zip asset

Open versions.csv in any of those directories to find a build’s version, the earliest version that recorded identical contents there, and the snapshot identifier. The matching files-<snapshot>.csv lists relative filenames and their MD5 hashes. A directory that returns to an earlier state reuses the same list. projr can also read a legacy root manifest.csv and imports its history on the next production build.

Run projr_manifest_changes() in the checkout to compare two builds, or projr_manifest_file_history() to see when an individual file changed. An archive records the builds it received, so its first copy of a file list can have a different version. For a worked example with a published archive, see restoring an earlier build.

Saving artifacts

Use remotes to give an archive a name and record where it lives. Use build.dest to select which archives a production build writes to. This example keeps a complete local archive called shared and sends just the figures to a GitHub repository. The project declares output-figures under directories.

remotes:
  local:
    shared:
      path: ../team-archives/study
  github:
    reports:
      repo: research-team/study-results
      tag: "figures-@branch"
      structure: archive
      send:
        cue: if-change
        inspect: manifest
        strategy: sync-diff
build:
  dest:
    shared:
    reports:
      content: [output-figures]

build.dest takes one of three forms.

build.dest What a production build sends
dest: shared All declared raw, output and docs labels to one archive. Cache is included only when explicitly selected.
dest: [shared, reports] All of those labels to each listed archive.
A mapping Each key is an archive name or a setting. A setting (content, cue, inspect or strategy) applies to every listed archive. Settings under an archive’s name apply to that archive only.

A per-archive setting takes precedence over a setting for the whole of build.dest, which takes precedence over remotes.<type>.<title>.send. An archive left out of build.dest receives nothing, but its saved files remain available to readers. Readers can ask for any label actually saved for a build, even after its publishing selection changes. A profile’s build.dest replaces the default selection, so dest: [] in a profile turns uploads off.

Name an archive by its title when no other type uses that title, or as <type>:<title>, for example github:reports. The words content, cue, inspect, strategy, conflict and version cannot be archive titles.

For GitHub, repo defaults to the repository that produced the build. The name under remotes.github supplies the release tag and title unless tag supplies a different name. For example, reports: {} under remotes.github registers a release named reports in the producer’s repository. repo: research-team/study-results sends the files to a separate repository. A release such as figures-main can hold files from several project versions.

Field under remotes.<type>.<title> Values and effect
path Local archive path, relative to the project root or absolute.
repo GitHub repository in owner/repo form. Defaults to the repository where the analysis is built.
structure archive (default) stores versioned payloads. latest keeps the current payload for each label.
path-append-label Defaults to true. On a local destination, false lays out artifacts without the label subdirectory. A dedicated path per label avoids overlapping payloads.
tag GitHub release name, used for both the Git tag and the displayed release title. Defaults to the registered name. A literal archive shares one release across versions.
branch Optional GitHub target branch for a new tag. The branch must exist in the destination repository. @branch selects the checkout’s named branch. Reusing a release preserves its tag target.
send.cue if-change (default) or always.
send.inspect manifest (default) compares recorded hashes, file inspects the files themselves, and none treats the destination as empty for comparison.
send.strategy sync-diff sends changes and removes obsolete files. sync-purge replaces the remote contents, upload-all sends every local file, and upload-missing sends only absent names. Defaults to sync-diff, or upload-all with inspect: none.

For a one-off production archive, pass labels to archive_local or archive_github. TRUE chooses the available archive labels. always_archive controls whether those one-off archives are sent even when unchanged. The first one-off archive also registers remotes.github.archive: {} or remotes.local.archive: {path: _archive} in _projr.yml, so projr knows where the files went. It does not add the archive to build.dest.

Naming a destination for a branch or build

Directory paths, local destination names and paths, and GitHub release names can contain the following placeholders.

Placeholder Example
@version archive-@version becomes archive-v1.2.3 for build 1.2.3.
@branch archive-@branch on feature/foo becomes archive-feature_2ffoo. A detached checkout uses __detached- followed by the full commit SHA.
@uuid A fresh UUIDv4 for each build, shared by that build’s scripts, renderers, paths and release operations.

The build supplies the values for all three placeholders. For example, figures-@branch uses the branch of the analysis being built even when the release is hosted in a separate repository. The optional branch setting selects the commit for a new GitHub tag in that destination repository.

Quote a YAML string that begins with @. A placeholder ends at the end of the string or before a hyphen, underscore, period, ordinary space or path separator. For instance, "@branch/@version" expands both tokens, and archive-@branching stays literal. Ignore rules cover the configured path template across runs.

Archive layout and restore

Local destinations keep per-label histories under manifests/. GitHub Releases carry those histories in a single manifest.zip alongside the artifact ZIPs. In an archive structure, a GitHub artifact is named, for example, output-figures-v1.2.3.zip. An empty directory version can have an explicit empty marker. In a flat local latest destination the names manifests, manifest.csv, VERSION, and CHANGELOG.md at its root belong to projr.

To reproduce a checked-out build published to GitHub, run projr_restore() in the checkout. It uses the release named archive by default and restores the declared raw directory labels. It reads the checkout’s production version, or the most recent completed build in its .projr/BUILDLOG.md when on the follow-up development commit. Supply version = "1.2.3" for a specific build or destination for another release tag. It verifies every selected directory’s paths and MD5s before installing any downloads. Local changes and extra files stop the restore unless you explicitly allow replacement with clear = TRUE.

Run projr_source() to fetch the raw labels from their latest builds on the remotes registered under remotes. Supply label to fetch other directories and remote (a title, or <type>:<title>) to choose the remote. Without remote, projr uses build.source, or else the single registered remote that published each label. conflict = "remote" replaces local changes, including when the archive records an empty version. projr_content_update() is deprecated and now calls projr_source().

If a destination contained @uuid, find its concrete path or release tag in the Resolved archive destinations section of that build’s .projr/BUILDLOG.md. In an older checkout, projr can read a root BUILDLOG.md. The next build or restore moves that history into .projr/. The changelog stays at the root.

projr::projr_source(label = "output-delivery", remote = "local:shared")

projr_restore_repo("owner/repo") clones a repository and fetches its directories with projr_source(). Use projr_restore_repo_wd("owner/repo") to clone into the current directory. Both accept label, and type and title to name the remote.

Fetching raw inputs

Use build.source to fetch raw inputs from registered remotes before a build runs. It takes the same three forms as build.dest. By default each listed remote supplies every declared raw label. This example takes the latest survey files from a colleague’s GitHub release and pins the codebook to their build 0.6.3 in a local archive.

remotes:
  github:
    survey-team:
      repo: example/survey
      tag: archive
      get:
        cue: if-change
  local:
    shared:
      path: ../team-archives/survey

directories:
  raw-survey:
    path: _raw_data/survey
  raw-codebook:
    path: _raw_data/codebook

build:
  source:
    survey-team:
      content: [raw-survey]
    local:shared:
      content: [raw-codebook]
      version: "0.6.3"

Set defaults under remotes.<type>.<title>.get. A setting under build.source applies to every listed remote, and a setting under a remote’s name applies to that remote only.

get setting Values and effect
version latest (default), x for the latest build within major version x, x.y for the latest within that minor version, or an exact x.y.z.
cue if-empty (default in builds) fetches only into empty folders, without contacting the remote. if-change fetches when the remote’s snapshot differs. always fetches every time. never skips the remote.
inspect manifest (default) trusts the remote’s recorded hashes. file downloads and hashes the files. none skips the comparison.
strategy sync-diff (default) and sync-purge mirror the remote and remove local files it lacks. download-all never deletes. download-missing never overwrites.
conflict error (default) stops the build. local keeps local edits and remote replaces them.

Before any hook or script runs, the build plans every fetch, downloading only into a temporary staging folder. It stops on a conflict before changing any files, then installs the verified files before hashing raw inputs. A pinned version that is already in place needs no network access.

A conflict is a local file edited since the last fetch that the fetch would overwrite or delete. Fetch records are kept in the Git-ignored .projr/source/<label>.json and stay on that machine. A fresh clone has no record, so local files that differ from the remote count as conflicts until resolved. A LICENSE that projr writes into a licensed raw folder is not a local change. Production builds record each label’s remote, version and snapshot under Raw-input sources in .projr/BUILDLOG.md, and the console reports each update.

directories.<label>.source and a source field under remotes are no longer supported. Use build.source instead.

Run projr_source() to fetch outside a build or to resolve a conflict. Its arguments (label, remote, version, cue, strategy, inspect and conflict) override the configuration, and cue defaults to if-change. In an interactive session, a conflict asks whether to keep the local files, replace them or cancel. Otherwise conflict decides. If two registered remotes publish the same label and build.source does not choose one, name it with remote. version = "current" restores this checkout’s recorded build, as projr_restore() does.

projr::projr_source(label = "raw-survey", conflict = "remote")
